papers.title: Hydrodynamics of robotic micro-swimmers in confinement
papers.abstract: Inspired by seminal work by E.M. Purcell, we discuss the problem of predicting and optimizing the performance of autonomous robots swimming in confinement. Our approach is based on the explicit numerical resolution of the fluid flow induced by the swimmer, and it is validated experimentally on a cm-size prototype composed of a cargo head and a rotating propulsive tail. Using hydrodynamic scaling, we predict the performance of replicas of our prototype scaled down to mm- and sub-mm-size to test the feasibility of autonomous micro-robots navigating in narrow vessels. The main result of our theoretical, computational, and experimental analysis is that, while hydrodynamics seems to place no fundamental obstruction to the vision of autonomous micro-robots navigating in narrow lumens inside the human body, it does provide useful and strict guidelines for rational design at different length scales.

papers.title: Machine learning interatomic potentials and orientational defects in polymers
papers.abstract: Photopolymerization of acrylated epoxidized soybean oil (AESO) is a convenient model of a self-organizing process in a soft, bio-based material: ultraviolet light starts a free-radical chain reaction, the growing network releases heat, and the mobility of molecular groups changes on several time scales at once. We follow this process from two sides. Experimentally, the real and imaginary parts of the dielectric permittivity of an AESO:VDM (1:0.5) mixture with 3 mol% of the photoinitiator DMPA were recorded at 500-5000 Hz under an intermittent on/off illumination protocol, and the resulting time series were analysed with a sliding-window Shannon entropy and the Grassberger-Procaccia correlation integral. Both measures show that short light pulses at the start of curing trigger strongly correlated, collective relaxation, which fades as the network forms, leaving only localized reorientations active. We describe these reorientations as orientational defects and quantify their energetics with the MACE-OFF23 machine learning interatomic potential, using relaxed dihedral scans of five rotational modes ($\alpha$, $\alpha/\beta$, $\beta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$) of an AESO fragment. Compared with density functional theory (DFT) reference profiles, MACE reproduces the shape of all five profiles (Pearson $r=0.95$-$0.98$) and the hierarchy of barriers - from 2.9 eV for the constrained main-chain rotation, through 0.54-0.81 eV for the acrylate rotations, to 0.16-0.18 eV for the methyl and 0.06 eV for the hydroxyl rotation - while underestimating the barrier heights by 3-20%. A simple Arrhenius estimate shows that the acrylate rotations are the modes closest to the frequency window of the dielectric measurement.

papers.title: A Monte Carlo study of closely packed two-patch particles with frustrated interactions
papers.abstract: Recently it was found that closely packed two-patch particles exhibit rich orientational ordering behaviors, e.g., nonmonotonic changes of the nematic order parameter and double BKT phase transitions [arXiv:2509.03981]. In this work, we show that, with repulsive patch-patch, attractive patch-nonpatch and intermediate nonpatch-nonpatch interactions, there exist frustrations in the system of closely packed two-patch particles. To investigate the ground states of the system, we design a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm with single-defect propagation. The simulation results show that the ground states are disordered and the correlation functions decay exponentially with the distance. These results demonstrate that in 2D close packing one could design patchy particles to explore orientationally disordered systems.

papers.title: Kinetic theory of dry granular particles under simple shear: steady flows and relaxation dynamics
papers.abstract: We develop a kinetic theory for dry granular particles under simple shear flow using the Enskog approximation combined with Grad's moment method for moderately dense granular gases with the volume fraction $\varphi\le 0.5$. The collisional moments and stresses are expressed in terms of generalized hypergeometric functions, retaining all orders in the dimensionless shear-rate parameter within the adopted Grad closure. Within this framework, we derive a complete set of equations governing the kinetic stress and the collisional contribution to the stress tensor. The steady-state solutions reproduce the shear viscosity over a broad parameter range and improve the predictions of the kinetic temperature relative to the anisotropic Gaussian theory at the parameter values examined. Temperature still shows appreciable deviations under strongly inelastic conditions. Additionally, the theory captures the overall trends of the normal stress differences, while their quantitative accuracy depends on density and restitution coefficient. We further examine relaxation following an instantaneous reduction in $\varphi$ from $0.35$ to $0.20$ at a restitution coefficient of $0.90$. The theory reproduces the temperature and viscosity relaxation for this protocol.

papers.title: Effective strain energy of soft laminates: Beyond neo-Hookean elasticity
papers.abstract: Composite laminates can be designed to reach desired engineering properties such as low weight and high stiffness. This study concerns periodic media made of alternating layers of soft rubber-like solids. Assuming incompressible and perfectly bonded elastic layers, the effective mechanical response of the laminate is estimated by means of homogenisation theory. This involves computing the spatial average of the energy stored in the layers, each of which is in equilibrium and homogeneously deformed. The study is conducted for layers whose elastic energy depends on two scalar invariants, in general. Beyond neo-Hookean solids, explicit analytical expressions are obtained for a special class of Mooney-Rivlin materials, whereas approximate expressions are obtained for Mooney-Rivlin laminates and for Yeoh laminates. These stratified media can be represented by a transversely isotropic elasticity theory at the macroscopic scale. Based on these results, an approximate effective energy for laminates whose layers combine Gent-type and Mooney-Rivlin behaviour is postulated. It is then used to estimate the macroscopic instability threshold under pure shear numerically. Results show that the specific mechanical response of individual layers has negligible influence on the macroscopic stability limit if a certain proportionality relationship between their energy functions holds. Furthermore, in a pre-stressed layered medium under pure shear, the influence of the individual mechanical response of the layers on the shear wave velocity is found to be comparable to that observed in homogeneous media, within the same range of investigated situations. Finally, more significant effects may be observed in non-proportional laminates.

papers.title: Polar director structure of SmAP$_\text{F}$ phase of bent-core liquid crystals in thin planar cells with bias electric field
papers.abstract: We study the polar director structure in thin planar cells filled with bent-core liquid crystals in the ferroelectric smectic-A phase (SmAP$_\text{F}$). We analyze a continuum phenomenological model proposed in the physics literature and present proofs establishing the existence of weak solutions and conditional uniqueness of nonconstant solutions. We further investigate the qualitative properties of nontrivial solutions and examine the effects of a bias electric field, surface anchoring, and cell thickness on the polar director configuration. Our results are consistent with previous experimental and numerical simulations reported in the physics literature. In addition, our analysis reveals new parameter-dependent behaviors supported by our numerical simulations and extends results reported from previous literature.

papers.title: Strain-induced splitting of the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition in 1T-TaS$_2$
papers.abstract: The effects of uniaxial and biaxial tensile strain on the $\rho_{xx}$ and $\rho_{yy}$ components of the resistivity tensor and the commensurate --- nearly commensurate CDW (CCDW-NCCDW) transition temperature in 1T-TaS$_2$ are studied. At room temperature, uniaxial tensile strain increases the resistivity tensor components by a comparable magnitude both parallel and perpendicular to the strain axis. In the case of biaxial strain, up to 20~K decrease in the CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperature is observed. In the case of uniaxial strain, a new phase with two different CCDW-NCCDW phase transition temperatures is observed, the splitting exceeds 10 K. The occurrence of such a phase is associated with the transition of the CDW into the commensurate state along the tensile strain direction while maintaining nearly commensurability along the perpendicular one. The results allow to justify various models widely used in analysis of transport properties of 1T-TaS$_2$ in commensurate and nearly commensurate states.

papers.title: The two-level systems in cryogenic solids, or how to avoid stressful memories
papers.abstract: Structural glasses prepared by bulk quenching a liquid melt universally exhibit puzzling low-energy excitations commonly known as the ``two-level systems'' (TLSs). Recent studies indicate that ultrastable glassy films made by vapor deposition exhibit substantially fewer TLSs and, at the same time, are more stable enthalpically than conventional glasses made by quenching a melt. A similar phenomenon is observed in very stable glasses of model liquid mixtures prepared using swap Monte Carlo sampling. However, in a separate set of enthalpically stable solids, exemplified by amber matured over geological times, the two-level systems persist. In addressing this seeming conflict, we emphasize that a depletion of the TLSs, if any, means the configurational entropy of the material is lower than that of conventional glasses made by bulk-quenching a melt. Ageing does induce reduction in configurational entropy, but amber, we speculate, achieves enthalpic stabilization through increased bonding, not ageing. We separately comment on the discrepancy among existing predictions for the extent of cooperativity of the two-level systems. Several experiments are suggested to test the present picture.

papers.title: Mechanics of heterogeneous fiber networks processed by an active fluid
papers.abstract: Internally generated active stresses can drive soft materials into structures that cannot form under thermal self assembly alone. For example, a microtubule-kinesin active fluid can assemble and irreversibly restructure actin-fascin networks. Increasing the motor concentration of the active fluid results in networks with broad pore size distribution and heterogeneous bundle structure. We probe the mechanics of these actively processed fiber networks by applying local forces with optical tweezers and measuring the strain response around the probe. Displacement fields of actively-processed networks propagate over a longer range than compared to unprocessed networks. Furthermore, networks processed at higher motor concentration are stiffer on average, while also exhibiting more heterogeneous response. At large strains, both unprocessed and actively processed networks exhibit strain softening and plastic restructuring. These measurements demonstrate that tunable active fluids can alter both the structure and viscoelastic properties of materials.

papers.title: XPCS-Echo and broad relaxation measurements using a bunch-mode data acquisition scheme
papers.abstract: Echoes observed in the intensity-intensity autocorrelation functions [$g_2(q, \tau)$] is a powerful method for probing nonaffine deformations and yielding behavior of soft viscoelastic materials subjected to an oscillatory shear. Multispeckle X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) measurements of large number of echoes with high time resolution impose severe constraints in terms of the computational hardware and potential degradation of the sample. These issues are alleviated by implementing a bunch-mode data acquisition scheme in which the highest resolution frames or bunches centered at the echo peaks. In addition, by placing the bunches in an aperiodic Fibonacci sequence, $g_2(q, \tau)$ over a long time span can be measured with orders of magnitude lesser number of frames. The performance of these XPCS acquisition schemes is demonstrated using slowly relaxing model colloidal suspensions. Furthermore, an analytical expression is provided for the quantitative description of full $g_2(q, \tau)$.

papers.title: Surface Charge--Potential Relation for Spherical Particles in Electrolyte Solutions
papers.abstract: Predicting the relationship between surface charge density and electrostatic potential for spherical particles remains a fundamental challenge in colloid science. Because the governing non-linear Poisson--Boltzmann equation lacks a general exact analytical solution, researchers typically rely on numerical calculations or various semi-empirical approximations. In this paper, we overcome these limitations by developing a dual-asymptotic framework that provides explicit, closed-form expressions for this surface charge--potential relationship across the entire spectrum of particle curvature. For weakly curved systems, where the Debye length $\lambda_D$ is much smaller than the particle radius $R$ ($\lambda_D/R \ll 1$), a formal mathematical derivation rigorously establishes the Ohshima--Healy--White formula as an exact regular perturbation expansion. Conversely, for highly curved spheres ($R/\lambda_D \ll 1$), we employ singular perturbation analysis using the scaled particle radius as the small parameter. This approach provides a first-principles mathematical justification for the spherical Debye--H\"uckel theory, proving that its leading-order expansion remains asymptotically exact within the full non-linear Poisson--Boltzmann framework due to the geometric deactivation of non-linearity. Crucially, we map the exact limits of this geometric regulation, demonstrating how non-linear screening re-emerges as the particle radius increases, with the breakdown threshold governed by the interplay between curvature and surface charge density.
